title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E526 treats transverse vibrations of an elastic rod. The deflection satisfies a fourth-order equation in s, with spatial solution y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f) and ω = a/f. The sound (frequency) is proportional to ω²c√(2gb)/a². The present case (III) is the cantilever: one end clamped, the other free. Its frequency equation is cos ω cosh ω = −1. Euler writes it as sin Φ = 2/(e^{ω}+e^{−ω}), with ω = (2k+1)ϱ ± Φ and ϱ = π/2.

Previous page: the fundamental is ω ≈ ϱ + 16°45' = 106°45' ≈ 1.863. The modern value is 1.8751 rad = 107.4°. Euler rounds it to 3π/5.

This page, step 1 (third quadrant): ω = 3ϱ − Φ with sin Φ = 1/cosh(3ϱ − Φ) ≈ 1/55.7. This gives Φ ≈ 1.05°, which Euler says barely exceeds one degree and may be neglected. The modern root is 4.6941 against 3π/2 = 4.7124.

Step 2 (higher roots): the next roots are taken as 5ϱ, 7ϱ, 9ϱ, …, since the correction Φ decays like 2e^{−ω}. The sounds are therefore 9, 25, 49, 81, … times πc√(2gb)/(4a²).

Step 3 (comparison with case I): Euler observes that, apart from the fundamental, these coincide with the overtones of the same rod in case I. Case I is the free–free rod, whose roots are cos ω cosh ω = 1, i.e. ≈ 3π/2, 5π/2, …. In modern terms, the clamped–free roots are ≈ (2n−1)π/2 and the free–free roots are ≈ (2n+1)π/2. Hence the k-th cantilever overtone and the (k−1)-th free–free mode share the asymptotic value.

Step 4 (Scholion §34): with u = s/a, the general motion is the superposition of all normal modes, each with its own amplitude C and phase ζ:
y = Σ C sin(ζ + t ω² c√(2gb)/a²) · [e^{uω} ± e^{ω(1−u)} + (1 ∓ e^{ω}) sin uω + (1 ± e^{ω}) cos uω].
The upper signs apply when sin ω > 0. I checked these mode shapes: y'' and y''' vanish at u = 0 (free end), and y and y' vanish at u = 1 (clamped end) whenever cos ω = −1/cosh ω and sin ω = ±tanh ω. So the formula is a correct closed form of the cantilever eigenfunctions, with the free end at s = 0.
errors: Euler says Φ in the third quadrant scarcely exceeds one degree. The true value is ≈1.05° (0.0183 rad), so the statement is essentially right and the neglect is harmless.
Printed misprint: the third sound is set as 49πc√(2gb)/(4ba); it should be 4aa.
Printed misprint in the second term of the Scholion: the cosine coefficient reads (1 ± e^{ω}) where it should be (1 ± e^{ω'}).

The opening phrase 'et quia angulus φ negligi potest, hinc sequitur … angulum φ vix unum gradum superare' is logically inverted (circular) as written. The intended sense is that φ is under one degree and may therefore be neglected.

ideas.what: Asymptotic roots of the cantilever frequency equation cos ω cosh ω = −1, approximately (2n−1)π/2, with an exponentially small correction
ideas.modern_name: Asymptotic eigenvalues of the Euler–Bernoulli clamped–free beam

ideas.where_published: E65 Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I; E526 itself

ideas.what: Overtones of the cantilever beyond the fundamental coincide with the free–free overtones
ideas.modern_name: Asymptotic coincidence of clamped–free and free–free beam eigenfrequencies
ideas.usually_credited_to: Commonly noted in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound; implicit in Bernoulli and Euler
ideas.where_published: E526 (this page); discussed in Truesdell's 1960 historical study of flexible and elastic bodies

ideas.what: General vibration as a superposition of all normal modes with arbitrary amplitudes and phases, with closed-form cantilever eigenfunctions
ideas.modern_name: Modal expansion / superposition of normal modes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli (1753) for strings; Euler for rods

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard, well-documented material: the cantilever eigenvalues, the asymptotic match of overtones with the free–free case, and the modal superposition formula. All of it is covered in Truesdell's history of E526 and in Rayleigh. The only notable points are minor printing misprints and Euler's explicit acceptance of general modal superposition for rods, which is already known.
transcription_corrections: Third sound: the image shows 49πc√(2gb)/(4ba), a printed misprint for 4aa. The transcription faithfully reproduces it.

Opening clause: the page uses the symbol φ (Φ on the previous page) consistently. In the third Scholion term, the image's 'e^{ω''}' is rendered correctly. In the second term, the original indeed prints e^{ω} instead of e^{ω'}.
